NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE IX: REPAIR, FAIRNESS AND MANY FUTURES (LCI-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume V concepts (401-500), the 30 themes and the five deeper subjects: old wrongs and their repair, who is heard, prejudice and fairness, care for minds and bodies, animals and hard tradeoffs, inventions and bad inventions, family life, and an island that keeps choosing its own future.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A teacher at the open lessons will not share their best remedy: urge them to share, or respect their choice.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has started lessons under the old fig tree, open to anyone of any age: fishing knots, star names, counting, herbs. One day a student challenged (friend), who teaches herbs, on something (friend.he/she) said, and (friend) stormed off. Now (friend) refuses to teach (friend.his/her) best remedy at all. What should (subject) do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) talks to (friend) about how questions are not insults, and how knowledge kept is knowledge lost. (friend) comes back, stiffly. The student apologizes for being rude, not for asking. (friend) teaches the remedy.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) lets (friend) keep the remedy. (friend) teaches it, eventually, to one apprentice of (friend.his/her) own choosing. The lessons under the tree go on without it. The student who asked the question becomes the best herbalist in the village anyway.
